title: Week in Review
vibe: Sample data, all made up. The week agents got cheaper and everyone pretended they'd planned for it.
tldr: Agent pricing started moving from seats to tasks.
Adoption is still mostly pilots, according to a (fictional) survey.
Austin's AI scene got a new monthly meetup.

stories.spark: Half-price agents start a pricing war
stories.summary: Example Labs halved its agent price and moved to pay-per-task. By Friday one rival had announced a similar plan, according to its own blog.
stories.why_it_matters: This is now a trend, not a one-off. Expect it to come up in your pricing reviews.

stories.spark: Most agents are still stuck in pilot
stories.summary: Fewer than 1 in 5 surveyed companies run an agent in production. Cost and reliability top the list of blockers.
stories.why_it_matters: Supports a narrow, reliable first agent over a broad one.

stories.spark: Laptop-sized open model gets its first real tests
stories.summary: Independent testers published early results midweek. It does well on short coding tasks and struggles with long documents.
stories.why_it_matters: Good enough for cheap prototypes, not yet for production.

items.text: New free AI builders night starts next Thursday downtown.
A (fictional) robotics startup is hiring 30 engineers.

watch_next_week.title: Example Labs' pricing webinar
watch_next_week.detail: Listen for how they handle customers who use a lot of tasks.

notes: This is sample data for the demo page. Nothing in it is real news.
